description: We are Eagle's Forgotten Legacy, a BAUET team exploring NASA's forgotten equipment on the Moon and Mars. Our team includes Amit Kumar Podder (Research), Md. Moniruzzaman (UI/UX & Content), and Md. Shium Joarder (Software Development). We aim to bring space history to life through creativity and technology. We welcome teammates skilled in AI/ML, web or mobile development, storytelling, and data visualization.
summary:
Introducing Two Worlds: A Letter from the Machines, a novel scrollytelling application, which creates twelve interactive NASA space missions and their landings in real-time. The application includes Surveyor 3, Apollo 11’s Eagle, Viking 1, Mars Pathfinder, Sojourner, Opportunity, InSight, and Ingenuity.

Our solution to the “Abandoned but not Forgotten” challenge is the creation of an interactive story that transforms technical logs of missions into personal ones. It comprises six interactive chapters where each space object tells its story in its own voice through narration of its landing, engineering troubles, and last message. In parallel, the user is able to explore the true mission telemetry and scientific discoveries using a Machine Data drawer and a wireframe 3D inspector.

Why is it important? Retired spacecrafts of NASA on the Moon and Mars are often viewed as a pile of metal without taking into account the huge amount of data gathered by them that significantly contributed to planetary science. Our work transforms NASA Open Data and 3D data into a narrative and intends to preserve the legacy of space missions and inspire future space researchers, engineers, and constructors.
details:
WHAT OUR PROJECT DOES & HOW IT WORKS

Two Worlds: A Letter from the Machines is an interactive 3D website built for the "Abandoned but not Forgotten" challenge. Instead of reading a textbook or timeline, visitors scroll through six chapters where 12 historic NASA spacecraft and planetary sites appear live in 3D right in their web browser—including Saturn V, Surveyor 3, Apollo 11’s Eagle, Lunar Prospector, Viking 1, Mars Pathfinder, Sojourner, Opportunity, InSight, and Ingenuity.

As each spacecraft appears on screen, it tells its own story in the first person with synced voice narration—sharing how it launched, what challenges it survived, and its last message back to Earth. Visitors can click "Machine Data" on any slide to view real mission facts, distance traveled, and scientific discoveries, or open "The Machine Index" at the end to rotate and inspect all 12 3D models in full color and wireframe mode.

BENEFITS

- Easy to Access: Works directly in any modern web browser—no app downloads, logins, or VR headsets needed.

- Fun & Interactive Learning: Lets visitors hear each robot's story, inspect real 3D spacecraft models, and check real mission data in one place.

- Learn at Your Own Pace: Visitors can follow the guided story from start to finish or jump to any chapter or machine they want to explore.

INTENDED IMPACT

Many spacecraft resting on the Moon and Mars are remembered only as silent, abandoned machines. Yet every single one helped unlock major discoveries about our solar system. Our goal is to keep their stories alive and inspire students, teachers, and young builders to dream up the next generation of space exploration.

TOOLS, LANGUAGES & NASA DATA USED

- Web & 3D Tools: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, and Three.js / WebGL for real-time 3D rendering, lighting, and wireframe inspection.

- NASA Open Data: Official 3D spacecraft and terrain models from NASA 3D Resources, paired with mission timelines, facts, and discoveries from NASA mission archives and the Planetary Data System (PDS).

- Team Eagle's Forgotten Legacy: Amit Podder (Web Developer & UI/UX Designer), Siam Joarder (Team Leader & Project Researcher), and Moniruzzaman (Storyteller, Editor & 3D Model Collector).

HOW OUR PROJECT IS CREATIVE

Instead of talking about old space missions, we let the machines write a letter back to Earth in their own voices. Giving each spacecraft a unique personality—from the bold energy of Saturn V to the quiet determination of Opportunity—turns technical data into an emotional story people actually want to experience.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

- Smooth Performance: We optimized the 3D models and scroll controls so the website runs smoothly on regular laptops without lagging.

- Real NASA Facts: Every story line and Machine Data card is based on real mission dates, landing locations, and scientific results.

- Clear & Readable Design: We added chapter navigation, slide counters, and clean text contrast so the story is easy to follow on every screen.
